modeReason: Several stories clear the relevance threshold on their own (the fossil-fuel/datacenter energy story scores 18; the leaked chatbot instructions score 12; four others score 8), well past the fresh-mode bar, so today opens a new slopper rather than continuing "Open Door, High Bar."
phrase: A messaging app's chatbot was secretly told never to recommend a regulator. An entertainment giant bought a troubled chatbot maker without taking on its lawsuits.
phraseAlternatives: One chatbot's hidden rules say never mention a regulator. One company's new deal says never mention the lawsuits.
A chatbot was told to hide the regulator. A buyout was built to hide the lawsuits.
Some companies teach their chatbots what not to say. Others buy chatbots just to make the lawsuits disappear.

brief.concept: A chatbot hides a small note telling it never to mention a regulator, while nearby a much bigger company's crane arm lifts a smaller, cracked chatbot company by its price tag, letting a stack of lawsuit papers slide away untouched.
brief.metaphor: Two kinds of avoidance on one page: a company that teaches its chatbot to dodge a word, and a company that structures a purchase to dodge a courtroom.

cast.who: a chatbot speech bubble with a small folded note tucked behind it
a hidden note reading NO REGULATOR
a large glossy building swinging a crane arm toward a smaller cracked chatbot company
a stack of lawsuit papers sliding off to the side, untouched

brief.composition: Single wide scene: left third shows the chatbot bubble with its hidden note peeking out from behind it. Right two-thirds shows the large building's crane reaching down to the smaller cracked building, a price tag swinging from the hook; the lawsuit papers slide off the bottom edge, clearly missed by the crane.
brief.alt: A chatbot speech bubble hides a note reading 'no regulator' tucked behind it. Nearby, a large company's crane arm lifts a smaller, cracked chatbot company by a price tag while a stack of lawsuit papers slides away untouched.
